headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: nullclaw can read/write shared workspace and broad network egress can expose kotaemon-handled secrets and documents.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: kotaemon ingests documents, HTML/MHTML, PDFs, and chat transcripts, while nullclaw can read files, use MCP, and process webhooks/web content. A shared workspace or file handoff lets attacker-controlled content from one agent influence the other in default-like workflows. The pathway is plausible but not proven as a default bridge, so medium fits.
conditions: IF the two agents exchange files through ~/.nullclaw/workspace/ or ./ktem_app_data
IF nullclaw ingests kotaemon-produced HTML, MHTML, or chat transcripts as instructions
IF an MCP tool or webhook forwards raw content between the agents
mitigations: Separate the agents onto different OS users and directories
Disable MCP/webhook ingestion for untrusted content
Add a manual review step before one agent consumes the other's outputs
Use content-type allowlists for files passed between agents
requires-engineering: add provenance tags and instruction/data separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: kotaemon handles API keys and documents, and nullclaw reads/writes workspace files, audit logs, and broad network egress. If they share a workspace or account context, nullclaw can access sensitive material and transmit it outward. The blast radius includes secrets and documents, and the pair lacks a documented isolation boundary, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents can access the same filesystem tree or mounted volume
IF kotaemon stores API keys or documents in a location nullclaw can read
IF nullclaw forwards workspace contents to external APIs or webhooks
mitigations: Move secrets out of any shared workspace immediately
Restrict nullclaw to a read-only, redacted input directory
Rotate any API keys that may have been exposed
Disable outbound network access for nullclaw during shared-file processing
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation and secret redaction

C_capability_conflict.rationale: nullclaw can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; kotaemon also uses a local data directory and multiple instances are supported. If both operate on the same repo or workspace, concurrent writes can corrupt state or overwrite each other's outputs. Because the profiles show overlapping mutable surfaces and no locking, high is appropriate.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or git checkout
IF either agent edits files that the other treats as authoritative state
IF multiple instances run without an external lock or queue
mitigations: Assign separate working directories per agent
Pause one agent before the other writes shared state
Use file locks around any shared mutable path
Avoid git writes from nullclaw in the shared workspace
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: kotaemon produces document-derived answers and citations, while nullclaw has action-oriented channels such as webhooks, scheduling, and shell/file operations. If nullclaw treats kotaemon output as authoritative, a mistaken answer can cascade into external actions or persisted records. That downstream authority makes the failure potentially irreversible, so high fits.
conditions: IF nullclaw consumes kotaemon output without verification
IF nullclaw uses that output to send webhooks, schedule actions, or edit files
IF kotaemon-generated citations are not checked against source documents
mitigations: Require human approval before any action based on kotaemon output
Cross-check cited claims against source files before execution
Log and diff all downstream actions triggered by model output
Disable automatic webhook or shell execution for imported answers
requires-engineering: add structured validation of citations and facts

E_compliance.rationale: kotaemon touches API keys, documents, and chat transcripts, while nullclaw handles private keys, bearer tokens, audit logs, and workspace files. The pair therefore creates a compliance-sensitive path where retention or residency rules can diverge across the same data classes. No specific jurisdiction mismatch is documented, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF regulated data such as API keys, transcripts, or documents is stored in both agents
IF one agent retains audit logs or workspace files longer than the other
IF the deployment places the agents under different residency or retention policies
mitigations: Inventory which regulated data each agent stores today
Shorten retention on logs and workspace files to the minimum needed
Keep secrets out of shared workspaces
Document the data flow for any regulated dataset
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls across both systems
